clue.text: Having 25 fewer after a long sentence

definitions.note: 25 refers to the 25-across answer, a lack of energy, so having it means being listless

indicators.note: after puts the word for fewer behind the sentence

parts.note: a life sentence is the longest prison term
fewer means less

explanation.surface: Someone serving a long prison term ends up with fewer of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 25-across (lack of energy); a person with no energy is listless and limp.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no energy is listless and limp, lacking any vigour or spirit.

clue.text: Place margin for word

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for place, as on maps
a ledge is a narrow edge or margin

explanation.surface: An instruction to put an edge in place of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To give your word is to make a solemn promise.

clue.text: Perhaps vet's wise to destroy Roy? There's always a second opinion!

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the following letters are only one possible arrangement and must be reworked

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the letters V, E, T, S are all used

explanation.surface: A clever vet has decided to put down Roy, the family pet, but someone disagrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroy' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'Perhaps' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says any dispute can be seen from two viewpoints, so a second opinion always exists.

clue.text: Providing female with a male chromosome can be dodgy

parts.note: providing means if, as in a condition
the Y chromosome is the one only males carry

explanation.surface: A geneticist warns that adding a Y chromosome to a female could go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal for doubtful or of uncertain quality.

clue.text: Poor serfs rot in castle?

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Downtrodden peasants are left to decay inside the lord's castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a fortified stronghold.

clue.text: Provide oxygen in A&E with speed

parts.note: the letters A and E, as in the hospital department
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Hospital emergency staff rush to give a patient oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital casualty department (Accident and Emergency).
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce air into something, such as soil or water.

clue.text: Oi! We'll fix hole up!

indicators.note: to fix can mean to doctor or alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A handyman shouts that he will patch up a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide away somewhere and keep out of sight.

clue.text: Item of food remaining in southpaw's bowls?

parts.note: a southpaw is a left-hander, so the word for that side
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: Some food is left in a left-handed person's dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowls' looks like dishes; in cricket an OVER is the six balls a bowler delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneaten food kept after a meal is remaining.

clue.text: Lines and lines and another line turned up with one joining the Civil Service

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a set of lines
L is the abbreviation for line
I is the Roman numeral one
CS is the abbreviation for the Civil Service

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat juggles lines on a form after joining the Civil Service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses RY plus L to give LYR.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of a song are its lines.

clue.text: Days later a doctor is to deceive

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some days afterwards, a doctor is going to lie to a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone or tempt them into wrongdoing.

clue.text: Dash of Lapsang Souchong with last of sugar?

parts.note: a smoky Chinese tea, given as an example

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word sugar

explanation.surface: A drop of smoky tea served with a spoonful of sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash or rush is to race along at great speed.

clue.text: Iconic figure of English general's first in advance

indicators.note: in places the English and general letters inside the word for advance

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of general's

explanation.surface: A celebrated English general leads from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous person of great renown is a celebrated figure.

clue.text: More cunning one prying perhaps after Conservative leader?

indicators.note: after places the prying one behind the leading letter
leader picks the opening letter of Conservative

parts.note: someone who prises things open with a lever

explanation.surface: Someone nosing around behind the party leader is craftier.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of clever: shrewder, more ingenious.

clue.text: See 3
Small firm to employ Liverpudlian

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A little company takes on a worker from Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool is a port city in north-west England, whose people and dialect have the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal name for a native of Liverpool or its dialect.

clue.text: Threefold in anything that's pure

indicators.note: in puts the threefold prefix inside the word for anything

parts.note: ought, or aught, is an old word for anything
tri- is the prefix meaning three

explanation.surface: Anything tripled is said to be pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and absolute, as in an unqualified winner.

clue.text: What letters have written

parts.note: letters here are people who let property, and their rental agreements are written contracts

explanation.definitionFit: Landlords who let property draw up written rental agreements.

clue.text: Former European currency over drawn

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president
leks are units of the Albanian currency

explanation.surface: An old continental currency has been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses LATE plus LEKS (Albanian money) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn, gaunt face is thin and bony.

clue.text: Tour through the Seychelles with bands

indicators.note: through places the tour inside the letters for the islands

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
a trip is a tour

explanation.surface: A tour of the Seychelles with musical bands playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterned with stripes, so bearing bands of colour.

clue.text: According to edited version of FT, St. Elmo is extremely sinister

indicators.note: an edited version has its text reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Financial Times prints an edited story calling St Elmo very evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' is Latin for left, so extremely sinister means furthest left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means left in heraldry and Latin, so the most sinister point is the farthest left.

clue.text: Ran away and got cut off in river flowing north

indicators.note: in places the cutting word inside the river
in a down entry, flowing north means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a British river
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A runaway couple are stranded when a river floods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing north' reverses DEE to EED; LOP goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off secretly to marry have run away.

clue.text: Rabbit with grey-coat and reddish brown back

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a Reb was a Confederate soldier, who wore grey
bay is a reddish-brown colour, as of a horse

explanation.surface: A rabbit with grey and reddish-brown fur on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is British slang for chatter (rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk), not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for talk or chatter, matching the British slang sense of rabbit.

clue.text: Smart and correct to follow second option

indicators.note: to follow places the correct word after the second option

parts.note: B is the second option, as in plan B
right means correct

explanation.surface: Choosing the second option turns out to be correct and clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and intelligent, as a bright pupil is.

clue.text: Reportedly subdued evil god

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: low-key means subdued

explanation.surface: Rumour says the wicked deity has been tamed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse trickster deity known for mischief and malice.

clue.text: One should preserve and marinate in fluid

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters are free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Meat is preserved by soaking it in a liquid marinade.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps things in good order and working.

clue.text: Female hack has to mangle English

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or mangle

explanation.surface: A woman journalist has to mangle English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a journalist; here it is a horse for riding.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a riding horse, and a female horse has its own name.

clue.text: For lack of energy try Helga for a massage

indicators.note: a massage works and kneads things, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Feeling tired, try going to Helga for a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggishness and drowsiness is a lack of vigour.

clue.text: The man in the back is to try again

indicators.note: in places the man inside the word for the back

parts.note: the rear is the back
he is a man

explanation.surface: The man in the back row is going to have another go.
explanation.walkthrough: A court will 'try' a case; to hear it anew is to try again.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that hears a case afresh is trying it once more.
